I have started a PR #37056 that extends fun_prop so it can be used to solve goals like HasFDerivAt k f _ x i.e. to compute derivatives.

Please throw at me whatever derivative you would like to compute so I can test it!

Would you accept an optimization problem? (in 1 variable)

https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.11396 links to work where the goal is to find the value of (integer) variable rrr with 0≤r≤m0 \le r \le m0≤r≤m to get the maximum value of 2−r∑i=0r(mi)2^{-r} \sum_{i=0}^r {m \choose i}2−r∑i=0r​(im​). Combinatorial arguments suggest r≈m/3r \approx m/3r≈m/3, and the paper refines it using a lot of combinatorics and little to no analysis. (The published version of this is cited in follow up work where an additional parameter ω\omegaω replaces 2 in the above, if the first expression is too easy for you. Currently it is hard to find the maximizing rrr for ω\omegaω sufficiently near 1.) Feel free to extend the function above to non-integers rrr in a way that makes a good test for you.

content: At this point I would prefer examples with a concrete Lean code, not some formula that I have to first reinterpret such that it makes sense to take derivatives of. I might have a look at it down the line but not right now

In probability files about moment generating functions I needed derivatives like this one:

import Mathlib

example {t x : ℝ} (n : ℕ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t ↦ x ^ n * Real.exp (t * x)) (x ^ (n + 1) * Real.exp (t * x)) t := by
  sorry

Rémy Degenne said:

In probability files about moment generating functions I needed derivatives like this one:

import Mathlib

example {t x : ℝ} (n : ℕ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t ↦ x ^ n * Real.exp (t * x)) (x ^ (n + 1) * Real.exp (t * x)) t := by
  sorry

With the current state of the PR you can do it like this

attribute [fun_prop] HasFDerivAt.exp

theorem hasDerivAt_from_hasFDerivAt {f : ℝ → ℝ} {f' : ℝ}
  {f'' : ℝ →L[ℝ] ℝ} {x : ℝ} (hf : HasFDerivAt f f'' x) (h : f' = f'' 1)  : HasDerivAt f f' x := by
 rw[h]
 apply hasFDerivAt_iff_hasDerivAt.1
 exact hf

example {t x : ℝ} (n : ℕ) :
    HasDerivAt (fun t ↦ x ^ n * Real.exp (t * x)) (x ^ (n + 1) * Real.exp (t * x)) t := by
  apply hasDerivAt_from_hasFDerivAt
  case hf => fun_prop
  case h => simp; ring

You can also define a simproc from the theorem

theorem HasFDerivAt.fderiv  (h : HasFDerivAt f f' x) : fderiv 𝕜 f x = f' := ...

simproc_decl fderiv_simproc (fderiv _ _ _) :=
  Mathlib.Meta.FunProp.mkFunPropSimproc decl_name% ``HasFDerivAt.fderiv

and use it as

example (t₀) : fderiv ℝ (fun t ↦ x ^ n * Real.exp (t * x)) t₀ 1
               =
               x ^ (n + 1) * Real.exp (x * t₀) := by
  simp [fderiv_simproc]
  ring_nf

Differentiating division that requires non-trivial discharger

@[fun_prop]
theorem HasFDerivAt.fun_div (hc : HasFDerivAt (𝕜:=𝕜) c c' x) (hd : HasFDerivAt (𝕜:=𝕜) d d' x) (hx : d x ≠ 0) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun x => c x / d x) ((d x * d x)⁻¹ • (d x • c' - c x • d')) x := by
  sorry

variable (hx₀ : x₀ ∈ Set.Ioo 0 1)

example : fderiv ℝ (fun x : ℝ => 1 / x) x₀ 1 = - 1 / x₀^2 := by
  simp (disch:= grind) [fderiv_simproc]
  ring

simp's discharger is passed to fun_prop when using fun_prop's simproc

Let me mention @Cameron Freer's tendsto_cont which is getting used in sphere-packing. The computations you're doing look more involved (to me) but more generally I wonder if something slightly more general is on the horizon here?

A silly example of computing limit of fun x => x * x at 𝓝 3

open Topology Filter
attribute [fun_prop out l₂] Tendsto

attribute [fun_prop]
  tendsto_id
  tendsto_const_nhds
  Tendsto.comp
  Tendsto.prodMk
  Tendsto.fst
  Tendsto.snd

  Tendsto.neg
  Tendsto.add
  Tendsto.mul

/-- info: ⋯ : Tendsto (fun x => x * x + 1) (𝓝 3) (𝓝 (3 * 3 + 1)) -/
#guard_msgs in
#check (by fun_prop : Tendsto (fun x : ℝ => x * x + 1) (𝓝 3) _)

However, I immediatally got into trouble when I used tendsto_const_pure. Having a concrete example of a computation you would like to automate would be very helpful.

I'm a bit sceptical if it can be useful for anything more involved than what can be done through continuity argument.

There's a bunch of tests here https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/blob/main/SpherePacking/Tactic/Test/TendstoCont.lean and some places it got used in practice here https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/pull/350
And the original spec here https://github.com/thefundamentaltheor3m/Sphere-Packing-Lean/issues/325
That test file is excelent! I will try the tactic on it!

Cool, fun_prop can solve all the those Tendsto test except

example (h : Tendsto (fun x => f (g x)) (nhds 0) (nhds 1)) :
    Tendsto (fun x => 2 * f (g x)) (nhds 0) (nhds 2) := ...

fun_prop does not support compound atoms/local hypothesis like that.

I defined a new congr lemma

theorem Tendsto.congr_l₂ {f : α → β} {l₁ : Filter α} {l₂ l₂' : Filter β}
  (t : Tendsto f l₁ l₂) (h : l₂' = l₂) : Tendsto f l₁ l₂' := h ▸ t

and all the proofs look like

  apply Tendsto.congr_l₂
  · fun_prop
  · first | simp | norm_num | grind | ring_nf

One interesting thing is that I had to reorder arguments in the composition theorem to

theorem Tendsto.comp' {f : α → β} {g : β → γ} {x : Filter α} {y : Filter β} {z : Filter γ}
    (hf : Tendsto f x y) (hg : Tendsto g y z) : Tendsto (g ∘ f) x z := fun _ hs => hf (hg hs)

i.e. hg and hf swapped places as fun_prop tries to solve hf first which will determine y and then it can prove hg.

Ok I think PRs are more or less ready

  • extension to fun_prop to support output arguments #37056
  • set up HasFDerivAt #37231
  • set up HasDerivAt #37270

Should I also set up Mapsto and Tensto with fun_prop? Anyone has some nice Mapsto examples that one might want to calculate?

Nice! This revealed that priority for fun_prop theorems is necessary. Right now, it uses HasDerivAt.fun_pow' rather than HasDerivAt.fun_pow and you get a really messy result with sums.

I added extra PR #37365 which adds support for tagging theorems with priority.

@Tomas Skrivan and @Cameron Freer I think it would be wise for you to coordinate to prevent duplicated work here. I think Tomas' tactic is more general, but Cameron's might be more powerful in the TendsTo case, particularly with spherepacking#378 (but I could be wrong!)
Thanks, that's a good idea. I also recently added a draft PR spherepacking#384, but will pause on this until I understand better what can be done with Tomas'.

Ok I make a branch that sets up fun_prop and Tendsto. I just went over the examples and didn't study your tactic outside of that. Here is the test file.

Few observations:

  • fun_prop can solve Tendsto (fun z : ℝ => z + 1) atTop atTop. It tries all the addition variants Tendsto.add, Tendsto.add_atTop, Tendsto.atTop_add
  • fun_prop can't work with compound atoms (h : Tendsto (fun x => f (g x)) (nhds 0) (nhds 1)) : Tendsto (fun x => 2 * f (g x)) (nhds 0) (nhds 2). What should be done if the goal looks like Tendsto (fun x => h (f (g (h x))) _ _, the tactic should somehow figure out that it should decompose it like h ∘ (f ∘ g) ∘ h. fun_prop does this decomposition independent of the local context.

A big part of fun_prop is to properly handle assumptions like Continuous (fun (x,y,z.w) => f x y z w) and correctly inferring that f is continuous in any subset of the arguments. I don't think that something similar hold for Tendsto.

I also had a look at few examples from spherepacking#384

  • in most of the examples within_disch := I get stuck on goals like 𝓝[Set.Ioi 0] 3 = 𝓝 3. So some extra care needs to be taken.
  • looks like that tendsto_cont prefers local hypothesis over tagged theorems. fun_prop is doing the other way around. I would say tendsto_cont is doing the right thing but does this come up in practice?

Hmm in general fun_prop seems to have troubles mixing nhds and nhdsWithin. I'm not sure yet if it is fundamental problem of the tactic, or just I need to pick the right set of theorems. I don't have any experience proving Tendsto so I don't have a feel for it.

1. I think letting Set.MapsTo and Filter.Tendsto be handled by fun_prop is scope creep for that tactic. I realize the former could come up as side goals, but those should be discharged with a separate tactic.
  2. I'm not sure this is within scope either, but having something that could compute iteratedDeriv would be nice too. Just today I wanted something to compute iteratedDeriv 2 (fun x : ℝ ↦ exp (- x • a) * exp (x • star a)) (where a is an element in a Banach ℂ-algebra) for me automatically. To be clear, this is NormedSpace.exp, not Real.exp or Complex.exp.
